Challis, C., Tierney, M., Todd, A. and Wilson, E. (2017). Human factors in dairy industry process control for energy reduction. Journal of Cleaner Production 168, 1319-1334. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2017.09.121

Locators are printed journal page numbers of the published version (PDF page = printed - 1318). Previously on the no-data path (background-no-data-extracted); extracted after the user ruling of 2026-10-07 that CTG033 is unobtainable and the Challis documents stand in for it. Every number is reprinted from the Carbon Trust IEEA Guide to the dairy sector (CTG033, cited as Carbon Trust n.d.): main file = two pasteuriser sites (regenerator 93% with 2.5 kgCO2/m3; 88% with 3.55 kgCO2/m3) and whole-dairy energy intensity by type from the Fig. 2 bar labels (liquid milk 32/175/391, cheese 127/412/484, mixed 55/373/1026 kWh/m3 raw milk best/average/worst); _measures = +1% regeneration saves 0.2 kgCO2/m3 (GBP 10,100/yr at 350,000 m3/yr) and excess water recirculation +16-18%; _other-values = Fig. 1 bar heights read from chart (pasteurisation about 4.0, CIP about 3.6, homogenisation 0.6, separation 0.5, intake chilling 0.4 kgCO2/m3), all-dairies range and sector shares. The accepted manuscript (30 pages) carries the same numbers (checked). The thesis challis_2020_001 Sect. 3.2 reprints this paper; these numbers are NOT repeated in the thesis extraction. Doubts: CO2 scope of the per-m3 pasteuriser figures not stated (likely includes indirect emissions from electricity); the paper writes kgCO2 while the thesis writes kgCO2e; the whole-dairy figures do not say final or primary energy, nor the carrier split; the text says best-to-worst liquid milk is a factor of 10 while the labels give 32 to 391.
